title: OpenAI Math Release Includes Claimed Progress on Three Millennium Prize Problems
summary:
OpenAI’s newly released math papers include a claimed proof of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis with a 7/8 bound, alongside partial progress on the Riemann, Hodge and BSD Millennium Prize problems. The quasi-Riemann result claims that all Dirichlet L-functions have no zeros where the real part exceeds 7/8 and that there are no Landau–Siegel zeros.

Will DePue’s breakdown of the collection also lists a claimed resolution of Hilbert’s tenth problem over the rational numbers and a Lean-formalized result on finite-time blowup for three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations with smooth forcing. Another listed result raises the lower bound on the chromatic number of the plane to six, advancing the Hadwiger–Nelson problem without fully resolving it.

The findings are part of 722 manuscripts grouped into 372 families of related results, produced by an internal OpenAI model that remains unreleased. The GitHub collection includes papers, proof artifacts and selected reasoning summaries. OpenAI consulted the independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence at the Institute for Advanced Study on how to release the results.

selectedTweets.text:
HOLY, the rumors were true: OpenAI has published 722 mathematical manuscripts produced by an *unreleased* internal model.

The collection groups them into 372 families of related results, drawn from an evaluation involving approximately 4,000 research problems.

OpenAI says the standard procedure used an average of three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result.

The release includes papers, proof artifacts and selected reasoning summaries. The model itself remains unreleased.
